text: ok so make the pipeline for us. we already have llamacpp but i assume that is unhelpful here since its diffusion. regardless, im not gonna go install a 3rd party tool just to generate a mesh and then export to import it if it can skip all those steps and just be put into our pipeline

events.text: Built genmesh pipeline: isolated venv (cu124 torch 2.6) at cart/hmsc-int/tools/genmesh/, genmesh.py (SD-Turbo text->image -> Shap-E img2img -> GLB), genprop wrapper that bakes via existing importPropMesh.mjs. Imports+CUDA verified on RTX 3060. Running first end-to-end fire-hydrant gen now (downloading weights).

resolution: Built and proved an end-to-end local text/image->3D prop pipeline (modly's idea, repo-owned). New tooling under cart/hmsc-int/tools/: genmesh/ (isolated cu124 venv on system py3.13 — NOT the box's broken conda env; genmesh.py uses Shap-E native text->3D for prompts which is volumetric, Shap-E img2img + optional SD-Turbo text->image behind --via-image for the future image-only backend, quadric-decimates to ~3k faces) and genprop (wrapper that generates then bakes via the existing importPropMesh.mjs, auto-bootstrapping the venv). Verified on an RTX 3060: 'fire hydrant' -> volumetric mesh (footprint 0.58x0.50m at 0.9m) -> baked as imported.hydrant, which props.ts merges into the editor catalog under the 'imported' category (placeable confirmed by source). Decimation cut the baked .ts from 19MB to 642KB. Backend is swappable; SF3D/Hunyuan3D are the documented quality upgrade. Committed a53abd7da (tooling only). NOT committed and left for the user's call: the 642KB generated imported.hydrant demo + Codex's still-untracked importPropMesh.mjs/importedProps.* subsystem. Not yet visually rendered in-game (wiring confirmed by source; user can confirm via their compiled loop).
